title: Cherrywood Chicken Thighs with Tamarind Gravy
description: Skinless thigh portions braise in cherry-smoked broth and finish in a mellow tamarind and brown sugar gravy.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: single-strength seedless tamarind puree
ingredients.note: Use pourable puree rather than concentrated paste.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 300°F with cherry pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {coriander} and {paprika} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Braise under cover
steps.text: Nestle {chicken} into the hot liquid, topping up with {topup} if needed to reach at least halfway up the thighs. Cover the pot immediately. No stall wrap is needed.

steps.title: Check the thighs
steps.text: Cook covered at 300°F for 25–45 minutes until the thickest centers reach 175°F and the flesh parts easily.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered chicken off heat for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Slice into soft pieces
steps.text: Slice across the grain and keep the pieces covered in a bowl with a little cooking liquid.

steps.title: Measure the sauce base
steps.text: Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Measure 3/4 cup into the HexClad skillet, topping up with {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Balance the tamarind
steps.text: Whisk {tamarind}, {sugar} and {aminos} into the measured broth until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Sauce the chicken
steps.text: Turn the chicken pieces in the tamarind gravy and spoon the extra gravy over each serving.

notes: Make ahead: Mix the tamarind, sugar and coconut aminos a day ahead and refrigerate. Option A uses tamarind. For gentler Option B, use smooth pear puree in place of tamarind and halve the brown sugar. Leave any added heat for the table. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Place one portion with its sauce in a covered shallow dish. Install the bottom drip pan in the APO and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, rear heat on, top and bottom off, 60% steam. Set the probe to 165°F in the center. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat until 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 214 kcal, 29.1 g protein, 9.5 g total carbohydrate, 5.9 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 180 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
